source.title: Forget Me Not: Fighting Local Overfitting With Knowledge Fusion and Distillation
source.authors: Uri Stern; E. Corn; Daphna Weinshall

page_placements.theme: Local forgetting can coexist with stable aggregate accuracy

record.file_problem: Full paper and appendices are present. There are minor OCR/formatting artifacts, but no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures test accuracy over training epochs, including a stated double-ascent result under label noise, and reports a model-size comparison. These are direct measurements relevant to epoch-wise and model-wise double descent, although the model-size results do not cover a full interpolation-threshold curve.
record.gate_note: The paper reports epoch-wise test-accuracy curves in Fig. 2 and a three-size ConvNeXt test-accuracy comparison in Table XI. Fig. 3a and Fig. 5 report forget fraction, not test error; these are recorded as findings that fit no version. Fig. 2c–d describe which clean/noisy examples are learned during a later ascent, rather than measuring the claimed curve, so they are not separate rows.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a methods paper (Knowledge Fusion and distillation). Section III still reports its own epoch-wise test-accuracy curves for ResNet18 on CIFAR-100, clean and with 20% symmetric noise. The noisy curve shows a clear double ascent; the clean curve shows none. These curves bear directly on epoch-wise double descent and on its dependence on label noise. The three-size ConvNeXt comparison cannot speak to model-wise double descent.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors say epoch-wise double descent is characteristic of label noise, with the dip co-occurring with noisy-label memorization. They report that a weaker 'local overfitting' (forgetting of test subsets) occurs on clean data while test accuracy rises. Their Knowledge Fusion of checkpoints, then distillation into one model, recovers forgotten knowledge and improves accuracy, especially under label noise.
record.recipe_differences: Measures test accuracy over training epochs and across model sizes on image-classification datasets. It does not report a systematic size sweep through an interpolation threshold; its main analysis also introduces a forget-fraction measure.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported epoch-wise curve differs between clean CIFAR-100 and CIFAR-100 with 20% symmetric label noise. Forget fraction is also reported as varying with model size and training-data fraction.

fits_no_version.finding: On ImageNet, forget fraction increases with ConvNeXt size while test accuracy stays roughly constant across small, base and large.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local forgetting of test points grows with model size even when aggregate test accuracy is unchanged.

fits_no_version.finding: For ResNet18 on CIFAR-100, forget fraction is significantly larger when training on 10% of the data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Smaller training sets increase local forgetting of test points; test error as a function of sample size is not measured.

fits_no_version.finding: Forgetting of test subsets occurs on clean data without global overfitting, across several architectures (Fig. 2a, Fig. 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Epoch-wise 'local overfitting' occurs without any global epoch-wise double descent.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (as stated in the supplied metadata)
record.problems: The epoch-wise curves relevant to the claim are shown only in figures, without numerical values in the text. The model-size comparison has only three sizes and does not state their position relative to interpolation. The data-fraction plot measures forget fraction, not test error as sample size changes.
record.rows_left_out: Fig. 2c–d report the clean/noisy composition of examples during a later accuracy ascent, not a separate test-error curve. Fig. 3b reports the last epoch an example was classified correctly, not a version's named measure. Other performance comparisons concern the paper's Knowledge Fusion/distillation methods rather than the double-descent claim.

untested.parts: All of it. The only size comparison is three ConvNeXt sizes, with no interpolation threshold and no error curve across sizes.
Other architectures, other noise levels, and test error itself. Only CIFAR-100 ResNet18 clean vs 20% symmetric noise curves are shown. TinyImageNet Fig. 2d shows clean/noisy counts, not a test curve.
All of it. The data-fraction experiment reports forget fraction, not test error.
Whether optimal regularization removes the peak, multiple or triple peaks, and variance as a driver. Only one noise level is compared against clean data.

missing.what: Mechanism evidence for the noise-driven epoch-wise peak. During the second ascent, mostly clean-label points are memorized, while the dip coincides with memorization of noisy labels.
missing.locator: Fig. 2c–d and Section III 'Reflections on the epoch-wise double descent'

missing.what: Architecture and training schedule for the Fig. 2 curves (ResNet18; noisy runs use cosine annealing with warm restarts every 40 epochs). Restarts may shape the double ascent.

record.verdict_notes: R1–R3 were relinked from V1 to none and the V1 verdict dropped: three near-equal ImageNet sizes cannot show model-wise double descent. The record's V2 'challenges' label for clean data is changed to limits_scope, since Nakkiran et al. also found epoch-wise double descent mainly with noise. R4 and R5 are additionally linked to V6 for the noise-dependence part. Most of the paper (Tables II–X) concerns the authors' own method and is correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: The model-size comparison covers only ConvNeXt small, base, and large. The text does not state where these sizes sit relative to the training-set interpolation threshold, and the reported range does not show a full fall-rise-fall test-error curve.

The plotted epoch-wise results cover the stated CIFAR-100 clean and 20% symmetric-noise settings, and TinyImageNet with 20% symmetric noise; they do not establish the pattern across other models or training regimes.
The training-data-fraction experiment reports forget fraction, not test error as sample size increases near an interpolation threshold.
The paper does not test double descent across model classes as capacity passes an interpolation point.
The paper does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.

Although it reports epoch-wise double descent with label noise and local forgetting on clean data, it does not test whether label noise or variance drives the peak, whether regularization removes it, or whether multiple peaks arise.
The paper does not re-express complexity using an effective parameter count or test whether that turns double descent into a U-shaped curve.
